course_name_original: English B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 2/3
course_name_en: English B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for FIRST-CYCLE students - semester 2/3
prerequisites: English language proficiency at least A-2 level.

learning_outcomes.text: Able to clearly present conclusions and opinions on general, academic and professional topics in written and oral form.

Able to use grammatical structures, phraseology and vocabulary that allow understanding general texts describing contemporary economic and social phenomena, academic and industry-specific texts, and allow for fairly fluent and spontaneous communication in academic and professional environments.

Able to write understandable informational and argumentative texts on general and industry-specific topics, conduct correspondence typical for the work environment, and independently use didactic materials.
Able to prepare an oral presentation on academic and industry-specific topics and participate fairly fluently and spontaneously in discussions, including in a professional environment.

Understands longer, even complex written and oral statements, e.g., lectures and presentations, provided they concern industry-specific issues and current affairs, and is able to interpret the acquired information.

syllabus_topics: Grammatical issues: Present Simple tense, Present Continuous tense, Past Simple tense, Past Continuous tense, Present Perfect tense, Present Perfect Continuous tense, Future Simple tense, Past Perfect Simple tense, 'be going to' expression, countable and uncountable nouns, adjectives and adverbs, verb forms – -ing and infinitive, modal verbs, conditional moods I, II, III, subordinate clauses of time, relative clauses, conjunctions, passive voice, reported speech, word formation.

Topics and vocabulary: Introduction and practice in various contexts of vocabulary and phraseology related to the following topics: studies: description of the faculty and nature of studies; career plans and job search; qualifications and character traits; private and professional interests; technological progress and innovations; latest industry achievements; company structure and functioning; regulations and instructions; employee professional development; official duties; finance; describing charts and presenting trends; phenomena and trends in the contemporary world; multicultural society; ethics at university and in the workplace.

Language functions: introducing oneself, greetings and farewells; receiving a guest at the university and in the company; conducting a conversation at a meeting, reception, conference; making appointments; telephone conversations; expressing opinions and suggestions; giving advice; inviting and accepting invitations; expressing offers of help and requests; seeking information; active participation in discussions on academic and professional topics; giving presentations; negotiating; describing using numbers and units of measurement and weight.
Other skills: writing emails; writing letters; preparing descriptions; writing argumentative texts.
assessment_rules: The condition for receiving credit is obtaining a positive grade from all colloquiums conducted during the semester. If a negative grade is received, the student has the right to improve it according to specific rules, including that an improved negative grade from the first attempt will be replaced by a positive one counting towards the average, while an improved grade from the second attempt will result in an average of the two grades (not less than 3.0 for a passed test). Unjustified absence from a test results in forfeiture of the attempt, and students have two retake colloquiums. The final grade is an arithmetic mean of all grades obtained from passing individual semesters and the foreign language exam. Admittance to the exam requires passing the compulsory language course semesters.
